QUIC connection lifecycle test with repeated connect, send, close, and cleanup.

# Purpose
This file is a QUIC connection test program. It creates one server `fd_quic_t` instance and one client `fd_quic_t` instance, connects them with `fd_quic_virtual_pair_init`, and then drives both endpoints with a simulated clock in `now`. The test opens a client connection, sends stream data, closes the connection, and then opens a new connection again. This loop checks repeated connection setup, stream send, stream receive, and connection teardown behavior.

The file defines callback functions for stream receive, connection creation, handshake completion, and connection finalization. The [`my_stream_rx_cb`](<#my_stream_rx_cb>) function checks that received stream data has size `512` and starts with `"Hello world"`. The [`my_connection_new`](<#my_connection_new>) and [`my_handshake_complete`](<#my_handshake_complete>) functions record when the server and client finish the handshake, and [`my_cb_conn_final`](<#my_cb_conn_final>) clears stored connection pointers when a connection ends. The [`main`](<#main>) function also creates the workspace, sets QUIC limits, configures callbacks, runs the service loop, and frees all resources at the end.
